column3: BOJ hikes to 1.00% at June 2026 meeting
column9: Base case per v1.3 update. Mark down 70% → ~57% on 2026-05-25 post April CPI miss. **Further mark down ~57% → ~50% on 2026-05-28: Tokyo May CPI core-core 1.6% (−30bp vs Apr 1.9%; 7th straight monthly decline), breaching the pre-registered 1.9% June-BOJ threshold.** Now a coin-flip. Why only -7pp (not a slash): (1) Tokyo CPI carries structural downward bias vs national from Tokyo-specific subsidies — national May core-core (Jun 19, post-BOJ) likely prints above 1.6%; (2) BOJ normalization bias is wage-driven (Shunto 5.26%), not spot-CPI driven (Ueda: temporary downward pressure won't prevent hikes); (3) counterweights intact: Q1 GDP +2.1%, exports +14.8%, 3-dissent split for 1.00%, Apr SoO "quite possible from next MPM." Against: Takaichi political ceiling; Sato joins June (hawk→dove); subsidies muddy signal; Iran MOU optimism. Threshold-vs-mechanism discipline: Tokyo CPI is a leading-threshold read; the wage-price mechanism is what the BOJ actually reacts to. **2026-05-29: April activity data beat (IP +0.8% MoM vs −0.4% exp; retail sales +2.1% YoY vs +1.4% exp) = hawkish counterweight on the mechanism side (firm output/demand feeds the wage-price spiral the BOJ reacts to). HELD ~50%, not raised — one activity print doesn't move a coin-flip, but it rebalances the split (soft price / firm activity), so the call is not drifting lower off the Tokyo CPI miss alone.**
